clue.text: Mate takes steps to provide communication between decks

parts.note: a mate is a companion
a ladder is a set of steps

explanation.surface: A first mate on a ship climbs some steps to pass messages from one deck to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' suggests a ship's officer, which fits the deck picture, but it simply means a friend here.
explanation.definitionFit: A companion ladder is the steep stairway on a ship connecting one deck with the next.

clue.text: See great changes in overseas accommodation

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of see great are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller notices big changes in lodging arrangements abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' turns SEEGREAT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest class of passenger berth on ships crossing the ocean.

clue.text: Join in a fortissimo number

parts.note: FF is the musical marking for fortissimo, very loud
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone is invited to take part in a very loud piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a piece of music beside 'fortissimo', but it is a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: To affix something is to attach or fasten it on, a synonym of join.

clue.text: Breaking foot, totters a bit

indicators.note: breaking means the abbreviation for foot is split open to hold another piece

parts.note: in British slang a totter is a rag-and-bone man, a ragman who collects junk

explanation.surface: Someone breaks a foot as they stagger about a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'totters' reads as a verb for staggering; it is a plural noun, the old British name for rag-and-bone men, door-to-door scrap collectors. 'Breaking' splits the foot abbreviation around them.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment is a small piece broken off something, so a bit.

clue.text: It's erected for the reception

parts.note: reads as a marquee put up for a wedding party, but means something put up on a roof to receive radio or television signals

explanation.walkthrough: 'reception' suggests a wedding party; it is broadcast signal reception.
explanation.definitionFit: A television or radio antenna is mounted high up to pick up broadcast signals.

clue.text: Matches in leagues

definitions.meaning: matches as in marriages or unions joining two parties
leagues as in pacts or confederations of allies

explanation.definitionFit: Alliances are unions or pacts, so both matches (marriages) and leagues (confederations) describe them.

clue.text: A good man in the mine, though too old for the job nowadays

definitions.text: too old for the job nowadays

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the word for the mine

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
ST, saint, is the crossword good man

explanation.surface: A good miner working underground is now considered too elderly to carry on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' suggests a possessive or an explosive; 'in' places the saint inside the coal mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone past it is idiomatically no longer capable because of age.

clue.text: Coach for trippers?

parts.note: reads as a bus for day trippers, but means a teacher for those who trip the light fantastic, i.e. dance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a charabanc for excursions; it is a tutor, and 'trippers' are dancers.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who teaches dancing is a dance tutor, someone who coaches people who trip lightly on their feet.

clue.text: Not straight and with future too unsettled

indicators.note: unsettled means the letters of future too are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone frets that things are crooked and the times ahead are too unstable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' rearranges FUTURETOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of true is idiomatically misaligned, off the straight or level.

clue.text: Pack animal brings everything back around morning

indicators.note: back means the word for everything is written backwards

parts.note: all means everything

indicators.note: around means the abbreviation for morning is turned about

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for morning, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: A pack animal carries everything home around daybreak.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'back' and 'around' signal turning a piece end to end, one each.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is an Andean beast of burden used to carry loads.

clue.text: Oriental seen in Chinese city, having a sly look

indicators.note: seen in places one piece inside another word

parts.note: Peking is the old name for Beijing
Oriental means eastern, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: An Easterner visiting a Chinese city is spotted glancing around furtively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' puts E inside PEKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Peeking means glancing quickly and furtively, a sly look.

clue.text: Dot three i's perhaps, many find it silly

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of dot and three i's may be rearranged

parts.note: three i's are III
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it foolish to put dots over three letter i's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges DOTIII into IDIOTI, then C follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic means foolish or stupid, a synonym of silly.

clue.text: Cattle without water

definitions.meaning: an old word for cattle or oxen
a drink taken undiluted, with no water added

explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an archaic word for oxen, and a spirit served neat is drunk undiluted.

clue.text: Capital footwear

definitions.meaning: the capital city of New Zealand
a rubber boot, named after the Duke

explanation.definitionFit: Wellington is New Zealand's capital, and a wellington is a waterproof rubber boot.

clue.text: An arm put round a pretty girl in game

indicators.note: put round means the girl encircles the other pieces

parts.note: a belle is a pretty girl
a gat is a gun, a firearm

explanation.surface: In a game, someone puts an arm around an attractive girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' looks like a limb but is a weapon, American slang for a gun; 'put round' has the girl surround it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a table game in which balls are struck into scoring holes.

clue.text: Play an exaggerated role in a covert organisation

indicators.note: organisation means the letters of a covert are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hams it up while working undercover for a secret outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' reads as a secret agency, but it means arranging ACOVERT afresh.
explanation.definitionFit: To overact is to perform a part in an exaggerated way.

clue.text: One is not bound to enjoy this

definitions.text: One is not bound to enjoy this

parts.words: One is not bound to enjoy this
parts.note: reads as something one need not like, but describes the state of not being tied up, liberty

explanation.walkthrough: 'not bound to' seems to mean not obliged; it means not tied.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberty is the condition of someone who is unrestrained and not tied up.

clue.text: The author is not in

definitions.meaning: Henry ..., eighteenth-century novelist of Tom Jones
in cricket the side not batting, i.e. not in, is in the field

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side that is not 'in' (batting) is out in the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Fielding wrote Tom Jones, and in cricket the team not batting is in the field.

clue.text: Straightening bandages

definitions.meaning: as soldiers straighten lines on parade

explanation.definitionFit: Dressing ranks means aligning soldiers, and dressings are the coverings applied to wounds.

clue.text: Their union offers security

parts.note: reads as a marriage giving stability, but describes the two pieces of hardware that together secure a door

explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests marriage; it is a fastening device and the thing that fits it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fastening mechanism works only when matched with its fitting opener, keeping things secure.

clue.text: Company show displeasure with failure to accept responsibility

parts.note: to pout is to show displeasure by pushing out the lips

explanation.surface: A firm sulks at someone dodging blame.
explanation.definitionFit: A cop-out is an evasion, ducking a duty or commitment.

clue.text: Order posted by a tyrant

indicators.note: order means the letters of posted are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A dictator sends out a decree by post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command from the tyrant but rearranges POSTED.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler who wields power cruelly, a synonym of tyrant.

clue.text: Rigid forms of worship

parts.note: reads as strict religious rituals, but forms are benches, so hard benches in a church

explanation.walkthrough: A 'form' is also a long bench, so these are hard church benches.
explanation.definitionFit: Church benches are long hard seats, a form being an old word for a bench.

clue.text: Waves on the pools

definitions.meaning: hairdressing curls set in the hair
permutations of matches entered on British football pools coupons

explanation.walkthrough: The football pools are a British weekly betting game on match results; a perm is a set of permuted selections.
explanation.definitionFit: Perms are permanent waves in hair and also permutations of predictions on football pools coupons.

clue.text: Lower speeds ordered on both sides of the river

indicators.note: on both sides of means the rearranged letters surround the river letter
ordered means the letters of speeds are rearranged

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Speeds are reduced by decree on each bank of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' turns SPEEDS into DEPESS, and 'on both sides of' puts it round R.
explanation.definitionFit: To depress something is to push it down, so lower it.

clue.text: She puts on other people's clothes

definitions.text: She puts on other people's clothes

parts.words: She puts on other people's clothes
parts.note: reads as someone wearing borrowed garments, but describes a theatre helper who dresses actors

explanation.walkthrough: 'puts on' seems to mean wearing herself; it means putting garments onto others.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre, the person who helps performers into their costumes has this job title.

clue.text: Peer in uniform

definitions.meaning: a peer is someone of the same standing, a match
uniform meaning even and alike throughout

explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a person of equal standing, and things uniform are identical in measure.

clue.text: They add grace to manners, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that to manners may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Good etiquette is improved by refinements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges TOMANNERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornaments are decorations that embellish and beautify whatever they are added to.
